nodes.summary: A family $A_1, \dots, A_t$ of subsets of $\{1, \dots, v\}$ is a $2$-design (also called a pairwise balanced design or a linear space) when every block $A_i$ has at least two points and every pair of distinct points of $\{1, \dots, v\}$ lies in exactly one block.
nodes.title: Linear spaces (2-designs)

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a prime power and $n = p^2 + p + 1$. Let $A_1, \dots, A_t$ be a $2$-design on $\{1, \dots, n\}$: every block $A_i$ has at least two points and every pair of distinct points lies in exactly one block. If $t > n$, then $t \ge n + p$.
nodes.title: Erdős–Fowler–Sós–Wilson gap above a projective plane (Erdős Problem 903)

nodes.summary: This is the statement that for every prime power $p$, with $n = p^2 + p + 1$, every $2$-design $A_1, \dots, A_t$ on $\{1, \dots, n\}$ with more than $n$ blocks has at least $n + p$ blocks. Here a $2$-design is a family of subsets in which every block has at least two points and every pair of distinct points lies in exactly one block.
nodes.title: Erdős Problem 903: line counts just above a projective plane

stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
